hidden_homeroom_d4_low.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d4_low.text: *In front of the meeting place, the homeroom teacher I run into pulls the worn paper envelope deep against her chest.* Sorry, but I can't show you the manuscript this time. See you at school on Monday.

hidden_homeroom_d4_neg.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d4_neg.text: *The homeroom teacher's face has gone cold as she shoves the paper envelope into her bag.* There's no manuscript for you to see. Go on back.

hidden_nurse_d4_low.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_low.text: *The school nurse pulls the zipper of the emergency kit she was organizing all the way shut.* I can finish this much on my own just fine. You go take care of your schedule.

hidden_nurse_d4_neg.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_neg.text: *Without even looking at me, the school nurse snaps the kit zipper shut.* I'll finish the rest of the organizing alone, so go on back.

morning4_start.name: {name}
morning4_start.text: *Saturday morning, the fourth day. Weekend sunlight slips through the curtains and wakes me. Instead of checking when to leave for school, I pull over the phone beside my pillow to check today’s plans.*

morning4_nightmare_seo.name: {name}
morning4_nightmare_seo.text: *A short buzz, and the alarm goes off. On the screen I turn on half-asleep, Seoyeon's name, the one I waited for all night, comes up first.*

morning4_nightmare_yuna.name: {name}
morning4_nightmare_yuna.text: *A short buzz, and the alarm goes off. Through blurry eyes, a message from Yuna sits quietly in the middle of the screen I just turned on.*

morning4_nightmare_dain.name: {name}
morning4_nightmare_dain.text: *A short buzz, and the alarm goes off. The moment the screen comes on, Dain's message, already full of energy this early, catches my eye.*

morning4_nightmare_after.name: {name}
morning4_nightmare_after.text: *Cheek buried in the pillow, I scroll slowly through the notifications that piled up overnight, one by one.*

minsu_cheer_1.name: {name}
minsu_cheer_1.text: *The moment I unlock the phone, Minsu's name glints on the top line of the messenger.*

minsu_cheer_1_b.name: Minsu
minsu_cheer_1_b.text: Hey, you've got a weekend date today, right?

minsu_cheer_1_d.name: Minsu
minsu_cheer_1_d.text: You spent all Friday in class in a frenzy locking in weekend plans. Thought I wouldn't notice? haha

minsu_cheer_2.name: Minsu
minsu_cheer_2.text: Dress properly. Don't wreck the mood. Do well out there haha

minsu_cheer_4_ins_single.name: {name}
minsu_cheer_4_ins_single.text: *I open the calendar app. The single appointment time in Saturday's box stands out sharp.*

minsu_cheer_4_c.name: {name}
minsu_cheer_4_c.text: *The appointments I overlapped, precarious as they are, are still there on the calendar. I already know too well this isn't something I can get past just by splitting the time, and my fingers feel heavy.*

morning4_start_2.name: {name}
morning4_start_2.text: *I open the window and breathe in the cool morning air. Instead of the timetable I checked during the week, I reopen the message with our meeting place.*

morning4_seo_msg_1.name: Seoyeon
morning4_seo_msg_1.text: Don't be late. In front of the park fountain, 10 sharp.

morning4_seo_msg_1_b.name: {name}
morning4_seo_msg_1_b.text: *It's one neat line, but the timestamp is seven in the morning. I can picture her getting ready long before, the way Seoyeon would, and a smile pulls at my mouth.*

morning4_yuna_msg_1.name: Yuna
morning4_yuna_msg_1.text: 10. Cafe in front of the station. If you're late, I just leave

morning4_yuna_msg_1_b.name: {name}
morning4_yuna_msg_1_b.text: *There's not even a period at the end of those two short lines, but I can already see Yuna showing up early anyway, sitting in profile by the window.*

morning4_yuna_msg_single.name: {name}
morning4_yuna_msg_single.text: *Past those plain sentences, I almost hear Yuna's quiet voice. I decide to give the whole day to just one person.*

morning4_dain_msg_1.name: Dain
morning4_dain_msg_1.text: It's finally today! You didn't forget, 10 in front of the gym, right? Ah, what do I do, I'm nervous already. Pretend you didn't see that last line!

morning4_fallback_msg.name: {name}
morning4_fallback_msg.text: *A quiet room on a weekend morning. I clear the notifications that came in overnight and set my phone down on the bedsheet.*

morning4_hidden_check.name: {name}
morning4_hidden_check.text: *Cutting through the early morning air, I wait at the crosswalk of the intersection in front of school for the light to change.*

hidden_homeroom_d4_missed.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d4_missed.text: *From inside the main gate comes the dull sound of an iron door closing. I swallow a disappointed breath, wondering if I was a step too late, and the walk signal turns green.*

hidden_homeroom_d4_1.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d4_1.text: Good morning. *At the half-open main gate, I come face to face with the homeroom teacher as she steps out, a thick brown paper envelope hugged to her chest.*

hidden_homeroom_d4_1_b.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d4_1_b.text: *The moment our eyes meet, she hides the paper envelope behind her back on reflex. Inside the thin wrapping, the printed manuscript stack rustles.*

hidden_homeroom_d4_2.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d4_2.text: Huh? {name}? What are you doing in front of school at this hour?

hidden_homeroom_d4_3.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d4_3.text: I could ask you the same. It's a weekend off, and you're at school this early?

hidden_homeroom_d4_3_b.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d4_3_b.text: The literature club critique was on the schedule, so I stopped by. I also needed to pick up the printout I left in the staff room.

hidden_homeroom_d4_3_c.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d4_3_c.text: *Instead of the neat suit I usually see at the podium, she's in a soft beige trench coat and a thin knit. The corner of the paper envelope hidden behind her back is crumpled small in her grip.*

hidden_homeroom_d4_3_d.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d4_3_d.text: You hold literature club critiques even on days off?

hidden_homeroom_d4_3_e.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d4_3_e.text: The members who signed up said a weekend morning was the only time they could make. An advisor has to fit the students' schedules.

hidden_homeroom_d4_4.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d4_4.text: *The joints of her slender fingers on the envelope flap are drawn especially taut. Through the gap at the opening, the first page of the manuscript shows a little, the marks of being folded and unfolded over and over still plain on it.*

hidden_homeroom_d4_4_b.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d4_4_b.text: Anyway, why were you hanging around here so early?

hidden_homeroom_d4_4_c.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d4_4_c.text: I had something to do nearby. I was just passing through.

hidden_homeroom_d4_4_d.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d4_4_d.text: For someone just passing through, you were looking inside the main gate for quite a while.

hidden_homeroom_d4_4_e.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d4_4_e.text: *Only the slow radio music from the gatehouse, carried on the cool morning wind, fills the space between us.*

hidden_homeroom_d4_5.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d4_5.text: The literature club kids went ahead to a cafe nearby, and the others will join soon. If you have time, want to watch the critique before you go?

hidden_homeroom_d4_5_b.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d4_5_b.text: I'm not even in the literature club. Is it all right if I sit in?

hidden_homeroom_d4_5_c.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d4_5_c.text: It's an open critique, and we take outside readers' comments, so that's fine. Whether you read the manuscript all the way through is something you can decide comfortably once you're there.

hidden_homeroom_d4_5_d.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d4_5_d.text: You don't have to feel any pressure just because your homeroom teacher wrote it. It's the weekend, so you probably have plans of your own. *She lets the sentence trail off, folds the paper envelope's flap over twice, and grips it tight.*

hidden_homeroom_d4_choice.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d4_choice.text: *Each time she steadies her breath, the corners of the manuscript rustle and knock together inside the envelope against her chest.*
choices: Sure. May I sit in on the critique?
I already have plans today.
You could have just asked me to come alone.

hidden_homeroom_d4_choice_trap.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d4_choice_trap.text: *She flinches and pulls the paper envelope tight against her chest.* I called you to a proper critique so there wouldn't be some pointless misunderstanding.

hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_1.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_1.text: See the literature club kids gathered at that long table by the window? The others will be here soon, so let's sit in this corner for now.

hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_1_b.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_1_b.text: You seem a lot more nervous than usual.

hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_1_c.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_1_c.text: Does it show? Honestly, I'm tempted to grab the whole envelope and run while I still can.

hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_1_d.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_1_d.text: Still, we ought to drink the coffee we ordered before we go. *She tries to pass it off as a joke and wraps her hands around the warm mug. Two round water marks overlap side by side on the cork coaster.*

hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_1_e.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_1_e.text: Which part of the manuscript are you thinking of showing the members?

hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_1_f.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_1_f.text: Now that I'm actually picking, it's just embarrassing. A sentence weighs completely differently when you fix it alone at night with the lamp on, and when you put it in front of someone else. *Even after she sets the mug down, her fingertips keep fidgeting with the ceramic handle.*

hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_2.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_2.text: For now I'm starting with the opening and the first scene. The rhythm of the lines the characters trade still worries me the most.

hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_2_b.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_2_b.text: Do the comments I write go into the official critique record too?

hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_2_c.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_2_c.text: I'll hide every name and only collect the comments. Where a reader's eyes stopped matters much more than who wrote it.

hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_2_d.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_2_d.text: *Through a gap in the homeroom teacher's leather bag, set beside the chair, the manuscript envelope shows. The crease is faintly worn with finger marks, from how many times it was opened and shut.*

hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_2_e.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_2_e.text: Do you know what scares a writer most at a critique?

hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_3.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_3.text: Facing the moment someone stalls and can't turn the page, more than a polite compliment. It stings the most, and that's exactly why it helps.

hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_choice.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_choice.text: If a passage feels awkward, or like you can't get a breath, underline it without holding back. Tell me honestly, too, whether you turned the page because you wanted the next one, or just kept reading out of obligation. *She points at the stack of critique printouts with her chin and looks quietly into my eyes.*
choices: You still haven't decided on the ending?
You'll show the whole thing to the club too, right?
The club members will probably say they like it because it's yours.

hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_choice_a.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_choice_a.text: Yeah. I still haven't closed the sentence on the last page. I keep trying to dress it up, and the real feeling goes blurry.

hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_choice_b.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_choice_b.text: Right. Everyone has the same printout. Write in pencil, so your handwriting doesn't give you away, and write however you like.

hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_4.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_4.text: Don't try to critique it. Just mark the sentences that stick with you. I'll mix them with the other members' critique sheets and read them carefully.

hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_4_b.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_4_b.text: *Waiting for an answer, her thumb keeps folding and unfolding a small corner of the paper cup sleeve.*

hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_5.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_5.text: All right. I'll write it honestly, in my own way.

hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_5_b.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_5_b.text: Should I leave my name off when I note in the margin? I'm afraid it'll put you in a difficult spot if the literature club kids recognize my handwriting. *At my words, she stops the hand that was smoothing the cup sleeve and gives a faint smile.*

hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_5_c.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_5_c.text: Thanks for thinking of that. Anonymous critique is the rule, so leave the name blank and just put down what you think.

hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_5_d.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_5_d.text: Does passing a manuscript around on the weekend count as an extension of school work too?

hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_5_e.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_5_e.text: On paper, let's call it club advising.

hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_5_f.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_5_f.text: *A literature club member waiting at the inner table comes over carefully and takes one more numbered copy of the manuscript.*

hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_5_g.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_5_g.text: I'll sort the notes gathered here, and we'll talk through them together at the next club meeting.

hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_5_h.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_5_h.text: Reading your writing in a cafe that smells like coffee beans, instead of the staff room, feels strange. *She writes a small number at the top of the last printout and slides it toward me. The fingertips passing the paper brush the back of my hand, then pull away.*

hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_6.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_6.text: Next time, let's meet calmly in the school library. I was in a rush, and I picked the place too suddenly.

hidden_homeroom_d4_decline.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d4_decline.text: Right. It's the weekend, so the plans you already made come first. I'll take the manuscript comments properly at school during the week.

hidden_homeroom_d4_decline_b.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d4_decline_b.text: *Checking a notification in the literature club group chat, she slowly turns and heads back inside the school gate.*

hidden_nurse_d4_morning_1.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d4_morning_1.text: I'm here for the counseling time you set last time. *I pass the hallway, messy with festival prep, and open the quiet door of the nurse's office. A counseling record and an information sheet lie neatly on the desk.*

hidden_nurse_d4_morning_3.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_morning_3.text: Right on time. Sit over here. Make yourself comfortable.

hidden_nurse_d4_morning_4.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_morning_4.text: *With a steady hand, the school nurse opens the counseling record and clicks her pen.*

hidden_nurse_d4_morning_5.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d4_morning_5.text: This is to wrap up the counseling we went through last time, right?

hidden_nurse_d4_morning_6.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_morning_6.text: Right. We'll see how you've been since then, and also settle a place where you can get help right away the next time things are hard.

hidden_nurse_d4_morning_7.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_morning_7.text: *The school nurse's eyes go down the checklist items she wrote out carefully last session, one by one.*

hidden_nurse_d4_morning_8.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_morning_8.text: Before I close the record, let's pin one thing down.

hidden_nurse_d4_morning_10.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_morning_10.text: *She turns the school counseling support sheet squarely toward {name}.*

hidden_nurse_d4_morning_11.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_morning_11.text: Have you settled on even one adult you won't hesitate to ask for help, even when the nurse's office door is closed?

hidden_nurse_d4_morning_choice.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d4_morning_choice.text: *On the printed sheet, the order is written clear: homeroom teacher counseling, the school counseling center, then the guardian contact list.*
choices: I'll talk to my homeroom teacher and the counseling center too.
I'm still not sure.
Can't I just talk to you?

hidden_nurse_d4_morning_choice_trap.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_morning_choice_trap.text: Of course you can come to me first. But there also has to be an adult who can look out for you when I'm out of the nurse's office, or when I can't reach you.

hidden_nurse_d4_morning_choice_a.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d4_morning_choice_a.text: I'll try talking to my homeroom teacher and the counseling center too.

hidden_nurse_d4_morning_choice_b.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d4_morning_choice_b.text: I still don't really know who I should tell.

hidden_nurse_d4_morning_12.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_morning_12.text: If choosing on your own feels overwhelming from the start, let's narrow it down together. First I'll highlight the extensions on this sheet that you can reach right away.

hidden_nurse_d4_morning_13.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_morning_13.text: I won't pass on what you confide to anyone else without permission. But if I see a risk of you getting hurt, I won't wait. I'll bring other adults in too. Promise me that one rule.

hidden_nurse_d4_morning_freetalk.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_morning_freetalk.text: *She gently closes the counseling record folder.* You remember the contact order we just wrote down together, right? If you hit a moment where you can't breathe, don't just endure it alone. Start with the place in the first box.

hidden_nurse_d4_1.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d4_1.text: *First-aid boxes for the school event and disinfectant tools are piled high on the long desk in the nurse's office. Sleeves rolled up, sticking on label stickers, the school nurse looks over her glasses and finds me standing in the doorway.*

hidden_nurse_d4_1_b.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_1_b.text: *Her eyes go wide as she turns.* Oh? It's a weekend morning, and you actually came to help?

hidden_nurse_d4_2.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_2.text: I put a notice up because I was short on hands to pack the emergency kits for the event site, but I didn't think you'd sign up.

hidden_nurse_d4_2_b.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d4_2_b.text: This time I'm here as a volunteer helping out, not a patient who came in sick.

hidden_nurse_d4_2_c.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_2_c.text: Good. A dependable volunteer for now. So much as cut your hand on the paper while we work, and from then on you're a patient again.

hidden_nurse_d4_2_d.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d4_2_d.text: I'll sort the sterile gauze and the alcohol swabs over here, where they're easy to reach. *Among the festival-prep staff hurrying in and out, I set the work table to match the way she moves.*

hidden_nurse_d4_2_e.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_2_e.text: *She sets a bundle of clear zipper pouches in front of me.* Two sheets of gauze and three antiseptic cottons each. I'll sort the papers with the students' sensitive health records myself.

hidden_nurse_d4_2_f.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d4_2_f.text: This row of pouches is filled to the count. Please check I didn't leave anything out. *Her fingertips and mine brush lightly over a pouch, and I pull the next empty one over right away.*

hidden_nurse_d4_2_g.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_2_g.text: Back when I was on a ward at the university hospital, getting stuck with supply prep like this alone all night happened all the time.

hidden_nurse_d4_2_h.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d4_2_h.text: You did all of that by yourself?

hidden_nurse_d4_3.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d4_3.text: You said there were coworkers helping beside you.

hidden_nurse_d4_4.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_4.text: On night duty, when emergency patients came flooding in, there were plenty of nights I had to run around alone covering three nurses' worth of care.

hidden_nurse_d4_4_b.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d4_4_b.text: So your body wore out, and that's when the burnout hit.

hidden_nurse_d4_4_c.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_4_c.text: It's true I was busy and couldn't sleep. But if I said I quit simply because the work buried me, the most important reason would be left out. *The moment she closes the file, the tip of the pen in her hand slips a little across the smooth cover.*

hidden_nurse_d4_4_d.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_4_d.text: What stifled me most back then wasn't the endless workload.

hidden_nurse_d4_4_e.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d4_4_e.text: If it wasn't the workload, what was so hard?

hidden_nurse_d4_4_f.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_4_f.text: It was when I caught myself mechanically checking the bed number and the vitals on the chart before a patient's face or name. I couldn't even tell anymore whether I was looking into someone's eyes or at a monitor.

hidden_nurse_d4_4_h.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_4_h.text: In the school nurse's office, there's time to look each kid who comes in straight in the eye and catch a breath. If it's something I can't handle on my own, taking them by the hand to a place that can really help is my job too.

hidden_nurse_d4_4_i.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d4_4_i.text: Does connecting someone to help count as part of treatment too?

hidden_nurse_d4_4_j.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_4_j.text: Of course. So if something gets too heavy to carry alone, knock. The nurse's office, your homeroom teacher, the counseling center. Don't just suffer it quietly by yourself.

hidden_nurse_d4_4_k.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d4_4_k.text: I've closed the zipper on the last first-aid kit. *Once the heavier first-aid boxes are set in order, the student staff who were waiting lift them and carry them out.*

hidden_nurse_d4_5.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_5.text: So I came to a school instead of a glamorous university hospital. I wanted to start over by learning to listen for what someone is holding back, before I hand them any medicine.

hidden_nurse_d4_name_choice.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d4_name_choice.text: *The school nurse pushes her glasses up and writes the number of finished first-aid kits, figure by figure, on the count sheet.*
choices: When are you glad you became a school nurse?
What's the biggest difference between a hospital and a school?
Serious injuries must be rare at school, so it must be less stressful.

hidden_nurse_d4_name_choice_a.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_name_choice_a.text: When a student who's been pacing the hall, holding it in alone, works up the courage to knock on the nurse's office door first. In that moment, I really feel I was right to come here.

hidden_nurse_d4_name_choice_b.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_name_choice_b.text: A hospital is where you're brought only after you're already badly hurt. Here, I can ask how you are before a wound festers. That's the biggest difference.

hidden_nurse_d4_6.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_6.text: Thanks to you working in step beside me, we finished much earlier than I expected. The story about my past is nothing special. You can just let it pass.

hidden_nurse_d4_6_b.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d4_6_b.text: What I just heard is absolutely not nothing.

hidden_nurse_d4_6_c.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_6_c.text: You listened so seriously that I'm embarrassed now, for no good reason. In return, I'll fill in your volunteer hours completely. Not one minute left out.

hidden_nurse_d4_6_d.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d4_6_d.text: *She fills the start time and the end time on the volunteer confirmation form in neat handwriting.*

hidden_nurse_d4_choice.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_choice.text: All that's left is sticking department labels on the outsides of the boxes. The event staff are going to the snack shop for snacks. Anyone want to eat together and finish the rest?
choices: I'll stay and label the first-aid kits too.
That's okay, I should get going
It'll be faster if you do it yourself.

hidden_nurse_d4_meal_walk.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d4_meal_walk.text: These are packed for the staff headcount, right? *At the snack shop in front of the school, I take the steaming bags in both hands.*

hidden_nurse_d4_meal_1.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_meal_1.text: Hold on. Who picked this spicy tteokbokki? Get some cold water over here, quick.

hidden_nurse_d4_meal_1_b.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d4_meal_1_b.text: You're the one who picked it up first just now.

hidden_nurse_d4_meal_1_c.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_meal_1_c.text: I tasted it first to check how spicy it was before the students ate any. *She downs the cold water in the paper cup in one go and wipes the corner of her mouth.* No matter how I look at it, even the digestive medicine in our first-aid kit couldn't save this.

hidden_nurse_d4_meal_1b.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d4_meal_1b.text: *After finishing the rest of the snacks with the staff, we come back to the nurse's office and stick area labels on the outsides of the kit boxes.*

hidden_nurse_d4_meal_2.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d4_meal_2.text: Your expression is completely different from when you were talking about your university hospital days.

hidden_nurse_d4_meal_2_b.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d4_meal_2_b.text: *While I'm talking and looking at her face, one label at my fingertips sticks at a slant on the corner of the box.* You look much more at ease now. Oh, I started talking, and the label went crooked.

hidden_nurse_d4_meal_3.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_meal_3.text: Right? Thinking about the old days, I must have gone stiff without noticing. Hand it over. Let's stick just that corner back on straight and finish.

hidden_nurse_d4_meal_3_b.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d4_meal_3_b.text: *I take the label she peeled off and press it neatly into the exact center of the last box.*

hidden_nurse_d4_meal_3_c.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_meal_3_c.text: Good. Prep stops here. Everyone check that your volunteer hours are written down, then head to the event area you're assigned to.

hidden_nurse_d4_meal_3_d.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d4_meal_3_d.text: *I grab my bag to leave the nurse's office, and she comes up behind me with a sheet of paper.*

hidden_nurse_d4_meal_3_e.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_meal_3_e.text: {name}, you're leaving the most important volunteer checklist behind.

hidden_nurse_d4_meal_4.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_meal_4.text: {name}. Thank you for working in step beside me from this weekend morning. On Monday, be sure to check that your volunteer hours actually posted in the school system.

hidden_nurse_d4_meal_4_b.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_meal_4_b.text: *She leaves a light smile and hands the finished first-aid kit box to the teacher in charge of the event.*

hidden_nurse_d4_pass.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_pass.text: All right. Just coming by on a morning off is thanks enough. Enjoy the rest of your weekend, and get home safe.

hidden_homeroom_d4_freetalk.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d4_freetalk.text: *She stacks the noted manuscript pages neatly beside the coffee that has cooled.* The literature club critique is more or less done. Now, what you really wanted to say. Shall I hear it?
hidden_homeroom_d4_freetalk.context: It is the morning of Day 4, just after discussing the homeroom teacher's old manuscript at a café near school. She appreciates the student's honest reaction, but they are still teacher and student. Use only manuscript facts revealed by the preceding scenes, and do not turn private closeness into a relationship that crosses the teacher-student boundary.
hidden_homeroom_d4_freetalk.personality: The homeroom teacher is careful and responsible, as both an educator and a longtime writer. Honest tension and relief show when she hears criticism, but she never demands comfort or secrecy from a student and guides the conversation maturely.

hidden_nurse_d4_freetalk.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_freetalk.text: *She zips the last first-aid kit, puts it in the box, and points a fingertip at the spare chair across from her.* Thanks for helping with the work. Now that we can catch a breath, I can listen to you for a minute.
hidden_nurse_d4_freetalk.context: It is the morning of Day 4 in the nurse's office, after preparations and first-aid kit sorting for the school event. They may have shared a snack or the student may have chosen to rest, so treat only saved events as fact. They remain a school nurse and student; trust has deepened, but professional boundaries remain.
hidden_nurse_d4_freetalk.personality: The school nurse is practical, attentive, and keeps her humor even when tired. She is honest only as far as appropriate rather than dramatizing her past, and she respects the student's health and choices.

morning4_end.name: {name}
morning4_end.text: *Back home, I straighten my shirt collar and my hair in front of the mirror, check the hands of the wall clock, then steady an eager breath and retie the laces of my going-out sneakers tight at the entryway.*

hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_trap.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d4_cafe_trap.text: Then there'd be no point in getting feedback. I don't want them going easy on me because I'm their teacher.

hidden_nurse_d4_name_trap.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_name_trap.text: I wish serious injuries were the only problems I had to deal with. More students keep quiet and tough it out.

hidden_nurse_d4_trap.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d4_trap.text: I can do it on my own. I was just hoping you’d help finish what’s left.

day4_haeun_concern_choice.name: {name}
day4_haeun_concern_choice.text: *Haeun turns toward me, her face set. The steps that were listening to her stay stopped in that same spot beside the school gate.*
choices: Ask what they heard
Not now

day4_haeun_concern_open.name: {name}
day4_haeun_concern_open.text: Haeun, will you tell me too what was said because of yesterday's talk? I'll explain all of it, nothing hidden, right here with you.

day4_haeun_concern_delay.name: {name}
day4_haeun_concern_delay.text: Haeun, I don't have time right now. Let's talk again later. *I turn to slip away, and a voice calling me from behind catches my step.*

day4_haeun_concern_clarify.name: Haeun
day4_haeun_concern_clarify.text: I didn't make up things that were never said to make you look bad, Senior. I only told them what honestly felt uncomfortable while we talked yesterday. *Haeun looks straight at me, her eyes steady.* If you meant something else, Senior, please say so here.

day4_haeun_concern_seoyeon_intro.name: Haeun
day4_haeun_concern_seoyeon_intro.text: *Beside a gate pillar, Haeun had been speaking quietly with Seoyeon. She sees me coming and stops.* I felt a little uncomfortable when I talked with you yesterday, Senior. I didn't know how to take it on my own, so I told Seoyeon.

day4_haeun_concern_seoyeon_arrival.name: Seoyeon
day4_haeun_concern_seoyeon_arrival.text: What did you and Haeun talk about yesterday? *Seoyeon slowly lowers the student council folder she had been holding.* It wasn't something I could hear and just laugh off.

day4_haeun_concern_seoyeon_escalation.name: Seoyeon
day4_haeun_concern_seoyeon_escalation.text: What bothers me most is whether you knew Haeun was that uncomfortable and did it anyway. *Seoyeon waits for my answer, calm, her eyes firm.* Don't dodge it. Say it here, directly.

day4_haeun_concern_seoyeon_escalation_de.text: What bothers me most is whether you knew Haeun was that uncomfortable and did it anyway. *Seoyeon waits for my answer, calm, her eyes firm.* Don't dodge it. Say it here, directly.

day4_haeun_approach.name: {name}
day4_haeun_approach.text: Haeun, can we talk for a minute? *I walk up to Haeun, who had been talking seriously with someone beside the open gate pillar.*

day4_haeun_finish.name: {name}
day4_haeun_finish.text: We were blocking the path in front of the main gate. Let's step into this shade for a minute. *I steady my breath and walk with Haeun toward the wall beside the gate.*

day4_haeun_notice_1.name: Haeun
day4_haeun_notice_1.text: *In the shade of the wall beside the gate, Haeun had started talking about Seoyeon. She trails off and fidgets with the knot of the bracelet around her wrist.* It's strange, isn't it. I opened my mouth to talk about Seoyeon, but whenever I come to, it keeps sliding into talk about you, Senior. I don't really know why I'm like this lately.

day4_haeun_notice_choice.name: Haeun
day4_haeun_notice_choice.text: *Haeun's unsteady eyes rest for a moment at the corner of my mouth, then drop to the edge of the paving stones.* Did my face just now look very strange?
choices: Pretend not to notice and check the clock
Ask why her face changed
Switch the subject to Seoyeon
Hear her out and thank her

day4_haeun_notice_up.name: Haeun
day4_haeun_notice_up.text: *Haeun blinks, a little startled, then flushes and smiles.* Thank you for hearing me all the way through without laughing. I still can't explain it straight out, but thanks to you, Senior, I feel a little lighter.

day4_haeun_notice_down.name: Haeun
day4_haeun_notice_down.text: *Haeun forces the corners of her mouth up into a smile and steps half a pace back.* Oh, right. We were in the middle of talking about Seoyeon. What I just said was only a passing thought to myself, so please forget it.

day4_haeun_reputation_cg.name: {name}
day4_haeun_reputation_cg.text: *In the cool morning air in front of the gate, Haeun waits for my answer with her lip lightly bitten.*

day4_haeun_personal.name: Haeun
day4_haeun_personal.text: Senior, could you spare a moment before you go? After we talked yesterday, there's something I thought about all night, on my own. *Haeun takes one step closer, under the quiet shade of the tree beside the gate.* Today, would it be all right if I talked a little about myself, and not about someone else?
